title: Organotypic Collagen I Assay: A Malleable Platform to Assess Cell Behaviour in a 3-Dimensional Context
protocol: Establish fibroblast cultures from 4 mm punch biopsies acquired from human forearm skin explants.
Place biopsy in MEM supplemented with 100 units/ml penicillin, 100 μg/ml streptomycin, and 0.25 μg/ml Fungizone.
Trim subcutaneous fat and finely chop the biopsy into small pieces using a number 24 scalpel blade.

Transfer tissue slurry to a 25 cm² tissue culture flask containing primary fibroblast growth media (MEM supplemented with 10% FCS, 100 units/ml penicillin, 100 μg/ml streptomycin, and 25 μg/ml Fungizone) until the surface of the flask is covered.
Incubate at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO₂ for 3 days.
Add 3 ml of primary fibroblast growth media after 3 days of incubation.
Change media with fresh primary fibroblast growth media or split cells 1:4 into fresh media if nearly confluent, omitting Fungizone from this point onwards.
Prepare collagen I from adolescent rat tails by washing the tail in 70% ethanol and removing tendons.
Remove tendon toward the distal region of the tail avoiding the sheath using toothed forceps.
Extract 1 g of tendon in 0.5 M acetic acid by stirring at 4°C for 48 h.
Centrifuge the extract (7,500 x g) for 30 minutes and discard the pellet.
Add an equal volume of 10% NaCl to the supernatant, and stir for 30-60 min.
Centrifuge (10,000 x g) for 30 mins, discard the supernatant, and re-dissolve the precipitate in 0.25 M acetic acid at a 1:1 ratio by stirring for 24 h at 4°C.
Dialyze the collagen solution against 6-8 changes of 6L ˜17.5 mM acetic acid (change 2 x daily).
Centrifuge dialysed collagen at 30,000 x g for 1.5 hrs.
Remove supernatant and place in sterile flask.
Adjust the collagen I concentration to ˜2 mg/ml using 0.5 mM acetic acid at 4°C.
Trypsinise the fibroblasts.
Spin the trypsinised fibroblasts at 400 x g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant from the spun fibroblasts.
Prepare 12 x 35 mm plastic dishes.
Resuspend the fibroblasts in 3 ml FCS.
Add the resuspended fibroblasts to the collagen mix and stir immediately.
Plate approximately 2.5 ml of collagen/fibroblast mixture per dish quickly.
Let the collagen set at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2 for 10 minutes.
Add 1 ml of fibroblast growth media (DMEM + 10% FCS) to each dish.
Detach the collagen/fibroblast matrix from the sides of the dish using a pipette.
The next day, add 1 ml of fibroblast growth media (DMEM + 10% FCS) to each dish.
Change the media every other day.
Allow the collagen/fibroblast matrix to contract for approximately 8 days until it fits in a 24-well dish.
Sterilize all forceps and equipment with ethanol before use.
Gently move contracted matrix using blunt forceps to a 24-well dish, ensuring it does not fold.
Prepare suspension of cells of interest at approximately 4 x 10^4 /ml after trypsinizing and spinning down the cells to remove trypsin.
Plate 1 ml of cell suspension on top of the matrix.
Allow cells to grow to confluence on top of the matrix for approximately 3-5 days.
Cut stainless steel grids to create a tripod.
Autoclave stainless steel grids prior to use.
Place sterile grid in 6 cm dish.
Add growth media to a level above the grid (approx 10.5 ml).
Place matrix on the grid.
Gently aspirate media so the bottom of the matrix is in contact with media but not submerged.
Replace medium every two days.
Live cell, contextual imaging using fluorescent cells can be performed at this stage or earlier.
Contracted or fibrillar collagen I can be imaged using second harmonic generation (SHG).
Samples can be imaged over the next 1 - 21 days to assess biological processes such as invasion, proliferation, survival, or differentiation.
Add 5 ml of 4% PFA in a Falcon tube.
Transfer the matrix onto a flat surface.
Cut the matrix in half with a fresh clean scalpel.
Lift the matrix with scalpel and transfer to 4% PFA.
Fix over night.
